arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Pincus argued that the government's position ignores mental factors.
Justice Scalia noted that criminal statutes often require knowledge of the act.
Justice Alito questioned the sufficiency of any threat of serious injury.
Mr. Katsas stated that the Act bars persons who assist in persecution.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests the scope of the immigration bar for persecutors. It asks if the statute demands a mental state or only objective conduct.

paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on November 5, 2008.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case seeks asylum benefits despite past participation in persecution.
The government seeks to deny benefits to anyone who participated in persecution.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues that coercion negates the intent required for the bar.
The government argues that the statute requires only objective participation in persecution.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The outcome defines the legal standard for asylum applicants who acted under duress. It clarifies whether intent matters in immigration bars. This affects how courts evaluate past conduct under threat.
